reason: The hypothesis relies on the formation of coherent, ductility-preserving carbides, but the cited evidence does not support this. E1 describes a different alloy system (W-based HEA) with different precipitates (δ/γ″), not carbides. E2 only mentions carbides as a general strengthening strategy and does not demonstrate coherent nano-carbide formation or ductility retention. The key premises about carbide coherence, specific strengthening magnitude, and ductility enhancement in the target alloy are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Coherent nano-carbide precipitates can be formed in NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 by adding ~0.5 at% C during mechanical alloying and SPS at ~1150 °C.
These coherent precipitates will enhance yield strength by 15–20% via precipitation hardening.
Coherent precipitates will maintain or moderately improve ductility by accommodating dislocations and delaying crack initiation.
The specific processing conditions (0.5 at% C, 1150 °C SPS, short dwell) are critical to avoid incoherent/coarse carbides that cause embrittlement.
